notes: Order is BLAST_GapAlignSetUp, BLAST_PreliminarySearchEngine, then merge of the local diagnostics; only this entry is called (prelim_search_runner.hpp:71; Blast_RunPreliminarySearch at 1609 is unused). The blastn CLI sets no interrupt callback, so no interrupt branch runs. LOSAT runs the preliminary stage over all subjects and then the traceback over the kept hit lists (CLocalBlast order). Setup parameters are compared in the blast_setup.c and blast_parameters.c ranges.

notes: bl2seq subjects come from the multiseq source whose total length is the sum of subject lengths (dbscan_mode), so db_length != 0 and BLAST_OneSubjectUpdateParameters is not called; subjects are visited in input order. NCBI skips only subjects shorter than 1; LOSAT returns for length < word size (process_subject, run.rs:6939) which is equivalent: the scan range is empty so no word hit exists, and the skipped diag-table offset advance is invisible in the output. equivalent: no word hit possible below the word size.

branch: db_length == 0 (environment variable BL2SEQ_LEGACY set; CLocalDbAdapter dbscan_mode false)
notes: With BL2SEQ_LEGACY set blast_app_util.cpp:206-211 builds the adapter with dbscan_mode false, the total length is 0 and BLAST_OneSubjectUpdateParameters recomputes eff lengths, search spaces and cutoffs per subject. LOSAT never reads BL2SEQ_LEGACY (grep finds none) and always uses the db_length != 0 path. BL2SEQ_LEGACY is not in the list of unset variables of the path scope.

notes: The subject HSP list (after purge, sort, merge and the preliminary e-value reap) is written once per subject in subject order; lists with no HSP are not written. bl2seq ignores -num_threads (blast_args.cpp:3216-3228, SB-635), so the NCBI write order is the input order. equivalent: LOSAT scans subjects in parallel but collect_prelim_hit_lists feeds the collector in subject order (E2f). hit_params->low_score is NULL for blastn (low_score_perc is never set), so the low_score update after the write does not run; the ungapped (!gapped_calculation) branch is out of scope.

branch: BlastLinkHSPParametersUpdate (link_hsp_params NULL for blastn)
notes: Blastn has no sum statistics so hit_params->link_hsp_params is NULL and the update, CalculateLinkHSPCutoffs (protein only) and BLAST_LinkHsps calls do nothing.

notes: Bookkeeping at the end of the subject loop (s_FillReturnCutoffsInfo fills diagnostics only; frees). BlastInitialWordParametersNew is called before the loop and is classified in the blast_parameters.c range; s_BlastSetUpAuxStructures has its own row.

branch: mask_type eNoSubjMasking (no lowercase subject mask)
notes: full_range = (0, subject length), hard_ranges and soft_ranges both the full range, offset = next = 0, sm_index = hm_index = 0; LOSAT builds soft_ranges = [(0, len)].

branch: mask_type eSoftSubjMasking (-lcase_masking, subject has lowercase)

A subject whose masks fall outside the range stays unmasked in both.
Allocation and restore of the subject seq_ranges between chunks; LOSAT computes each chunk's ranges into a scratch vector, so nothing is observable.

branch: backup->next >= full_range.right (all chunks done)
notes: Returns Done when next reaches the subject length; same test.

branch: subject not chunked (offset 0, residual 0, next == full_range.right)
notes: length = hard_ranges[0].right - 0 = whole subject, seq_ranges = soft_ranges (full range or the lowercase ranges). LOSAT uses SeqRanges::Inline(0, len) for an unmasked subject and SoftRangesFull otherwise. Subjects up to 5,000,000 bases take this branch.

branch: subject longer than MAX_DBSEQ_LEN, no soft mask
notes: Chunk length 5,000,000, next = offset + 5,000,000 - 100, offset = next - next % 4 (always 0 mod 4 here), seq_ranges = [(residual, length)] with residual 0; the last chunk takes the remaining length and next = full_range.right. Int4 sums cannot overflow below the 2^31 total length that LOSAT rejects. Unmasked chunks scan the full chunk (mask_type stays eNoSubjMasking so seq_ranges are ignored by the scanner and LOSAT passes masked = false).

branch: subject longer than MAX_DBSEQ_LEN, soft masked (lowercase ranges re-cut per chunk)
notes: start = chunk offset, end = offset + length; i = sm_index; skip ranges with right < start; take ranges with left < end; sm_index = i - 1; first left clamped to 0 and last right clamped to the chunk length after subtracting the chunk offset. NCBI's skip loop has no bound but the last soft range always has right = subject length >= start, so LOSAT's bounded loops give the same result.

branch: SUBJECT_SPLIT_NO_RANGE (soft-masked chunk with no unmasked range)
notes: Chunk is skipped (caller continues), hm_index and next already advanced; LOSAT returns SubjectChunkStatus::NoRange and loops on.

branch: chunk loop, WordFinder call, init_hitlist->total == 0 skip
notes: Each chunk gets a fresh init hit list, the word finder (BlastNaWordFinder, other range) runs on the chunk, and a chunk without initial hits is skipped before any gapped work, merge or best-hit filter. kNucleotide is TRUE so the residual is next % 4; dbseq_chunk_overlap is DBSEQ_CHUNK_OVERLAP (100) because Blast_ProgramIsMapping is false.

branch: gapped: GetGappedScore, Blast_HSPListPurgeHSPsWithCommonEndpoints(TRUE), Blast_HSPListSortByScore
notes: GetGappedScore runs on the chunk's sorted init hits, then the purge of HSPs with common endpoints, then a score sort (stable, as glibc qsort; skipped when already sorted, like Blast_HSPListIsSortedByScore) - same order in LOSAT. The odd-score rounding call is under #if 0. Purge and sort internals belong to the blast_hits.c range.

branch: hspcnt == 0 skip, Blast_HSPListAdjustOffsets, overlap, Blast_HSPListsMerge (subject split)
notes: Offsets of the chunk's HSPs are shifted by the chunk offset after the purge and sort, then merged with the running list using split offset = chunk offset and contexts_per_query = INT4_MIN. NCBI computes overlap after s_GetNextSubjectChunk has already advanced hm_index, so for the last chunk it reads hard_ranges[1] out of bounds (the seq_ranges pointer bits); the value is 0 only for an unmasked first chunk (seq_ranges NULL gives left = 0) and is unused for the first chunk because the combined list is still NULL, and it is 100 for every later chunk (a masked subject would need offset to equal the low 32 bits of the seq_ranges pointer). equivalent: LOSAT computes overlap 0 for the first chunk of a multi-chunk subject and 100 for every other chunk (a single chunk gets 100, unused); empty chunk lists are skipped by merge_prelim_hit_lists. Merge internals belong to the blast_hits.c range.

branch: -subject_besthit: Blast_HSPListSubjectBestHit on the combined list after each non-empty chunk
notes: Applied only when subject_besthit_opts is set, after each merge. LOSAT also runs it for chunks with no HSP; that is harmless because the filter is idempotent on a list it has already filtered (a survivor was never removed by any earlier non-NULL HSP, and removed HSPs never acted as containers). Filter internals belong to the blast_hits.c range.

NCBI frees an HSP when evalue > prelim_evalue (cutoff = options->expect_value) and keeps every other HSP; LOSAT keeps only when prelim_evalue <= evalue_threshold. They differ only when the cutoff or an e-value is NaN: NCBI keeps the HSP (NaN > x is false), LOSAT drops it. ncbi_double (value_parsers.rs:231) accepts a leading sign followed by nan (for example -evalue +nan). Ordinary values, +-inf and the -1 e-value of an invalid Karlin block agree.

branch: nucleotide, untranslated subject: contexts 1..1, subject->frame = 1, Blast_HSPListAppend
notes: One pass over context 1 (subject plus strand; query strands live in the query contexts), subject->frame = 1 (LOSAT subject_frame_sign = 1); the chunk list is appended to the empty subject list with kHspNumMax = INT4_MAX (hsp_num_max is 0 and never set), which is a plain transfer. Translated, RPS and out-of-frame branches are out of scope.

branch: link_hsp_params NULL: Blast_HSPListGetEvalues for all HSPs of the subject
notes: E-values are computed once on the combined subject list: round the score down to even when sbp->round_down, then eff_searchsp * exp(-Lambda*S + logK) with the gapped Karlin block of the HSP's context (no Spouge block for blastn; stat_length is unused; scale_factor 1.0). LOSAT applies the same formula per HSP with the per-context eff_searchsp. Formula internals belong to the blast_hits.c range.

branch: matrix_only_scoring false; empty list freed; diagnostics
notes: sbp->matrix_only_scoring is only set for reward 0 / penalty 0 (rmblastn), which LOSAT rejects (scoring.rs:check_losat_limits, reward <= 0); an empty list after the reap is freed and not written. Gapped statistics counters are not output.
Freeing of translation buffers, aux structures and filling of cutoff diagnostics; no effect on output, warnings or exit status.

branch: blastn / megablast lookup (BlastNaWordFinder), GetGappedScore = BLAST_GetGappedScore
notes: For a nucleotide lookup table that is not indexed, the scan routine (BlastChooseNucleotideScanSubject) and extension (BlastChooseNaExtend) are chosen in other ranges, WordFinder = BlastNaWordFinder, offset_pairs sized GetOffsetArraySize, init hit list new, GetGappedScore = BLAST_GetGappedScore. The word-finder diag table sizing from query->length (BlastExtendWordNew) is E2c section J. Smith-Waterman, jumper, PHI, protein and RPS branches are out of scope.

branch: task blastn (ePrelimGapExt eDynProgScoreOnly)
notes: dp_mem_alloc 1000 BlastGapDP, two prelim edit blocks, gap_x_dropoff = ext_params->gap_x_dropoff (the final X-drop is set before the traceback); chaining is off and jumper not used. equivalent: LOSAT keeps one scratch per worker and initialises dp_mem to MININT where C leaves it uninitialised (every cell is written before it is read).

branch: task megablast (eGreedyScoreOnly), gap costs 0/0 (non-affine last_seq2_off)
notes: Allocation sized from min(5,000,000, max subject length)/2 + 1 capped at GREEDY_MAX_COST 1000; LOSAT sizes from the current subject. The result does not depend on max_dist: BLAST_GreedyGappedAlignment doubles max_dist and restarts the direction until BLAST_GreedyAlign converges (return -1 otherwise), and a converged run is independent of max_dist. Two full-width rows (2*max_d+6) and the traceback pool are modelled in LOSAT including stale cells (E2c section H).

branch: task megablast, affine gap costs (last_seq2_off_affine, diag_bounds)
notes: Allocation for the affine greedy aligner: max_d *= GE_cost, diag_bounds, rows of max_cost+1; same max_dist-independence as above. NCBI returns -1 (an error) only if a malloc/calloc fails, which for gap costs near 32767 would need several GB (machine dependent, not reproduced); LOSAT rejects greedy gap costs above 32767 (see the rejected row).

branch: megablast gap open or extend above 32767
notes: LOSAT stops with 'gap costs above 32767 with greedy extension ... are not supported by LOSAT's BLASTN' because the NCBI 32-bit distance arithmetic (max_d *= GE_cost, scaled_max_dist) and allocations may overflow or fail.

Traceback state pool of ALIGN_EX (2 MB chunks, rows start at used+1, purge only resets used and does not clear). LOSAT keeps one Vec per row and reuses rows without clearing; traceback only reads cells that the same DP pass wrote, so the retained stale bytes cannot reach the output.

branch: task blastn traceback, left extension (reverse_sequence TRUE, q_start+1 by s_start+1) and right extension (start excluded)
notes: Compared line by line: x_dropoff raised to gap_open+gap_extend, num_extra_cells (x_dropoff/gap_extend+3, N+3 if gap_extend is 0), the first row of gaps in A, per-row first_b_index/b_size updates, script bits (SUB, GAP_IN_A/B, EXTEND_GAP_A 0x10, EXTEND_GAP_B 0x40), the MININT = INT4_MIN/2 sentinels, row growth, the traceback walk from (a_offset, b_offset) and the run-length edit block with the op adjacent to the seed last. The read of b_index == N (sentinel byte in C, code 0 in LOSAT) only feeds next_score that no later cell uses. FENCE_SENTRY (201) cannot occur in a blastn subject, so the fence branches are dead in both.

branch: score_only TRUE/FALSE
notes: Not called on the blastn path: the preliminary stage uses s_BlastAlignPackedNucl and the traceback calls ALIGN_EX directly (the Blast_SemiGappedAlign calls in BLAST_GappedAlignmentWithTraceback are commented out; other callers are protein and PHI). LOSAT's extend_gapped_one_direction (gapped.rs:981) is not used by the blastn engine.

NCBI finds the context of each initial hit by BSearchContextInfo on the seed q_off, subtracts the context start from q_off and ungapped q_start, and uses the context's query pointer and length. LOSAT stores the context index found at scan time and the context-local offsets (qs = ungapped.q_start - q_context_start; seed_q_off = q_off - q_context_start), and aligns the per-context query. equivalent: same context, same local coordinates.

branch: setup: hsp list new, interval tree sized (query->length+1, subject->length+1), restricted_align / chaining / low_score / RPS parts not used
notes: For blastn restricted_align is FALSE (only blastp), chaining is off, hit_params->low_score is NULL, is_prot is FALSE and there is no RPS or out-of-frame work, so only the HSP list (hsp_num_max INT4_MAX), the interval tree (concatenated query length + 1 by chunk length + 1) and the per-hit loop remain. An empty init list returns before any of it.

branch: precondition: init_hitlist sorted by score_compare_match (sorted in BlastNaWordFinder, na_ungapped.c:1692)
notes: The comparator (score desc, s_start asc, length desc, q_start asc) is copied, but NCBI compares the q_start of the concatenated query while LOSAT's qs is context-local (qs = ungapped.q_start - q_context_start, run.rs:8440), and LOSAT uses sort_unstable_by where glibc qsort is a stable merge sort. Hits of different contexts (other strand or another query) with equal score, subject start and length order differently: NCBI puts the plus-strand hit first (its concatenated q_start is smaller), LOSAT orders by local qs and, when local qs is equal too, arbitrarily. Example: a query X followed by the reverse complement of X (an inverted repeat) searched against a subject containing X gives such ties between its two strands; ties between different queries are split per query later and cannot show. The order feeds the HSP list order (ScoreCompareHSPs ties again, stable sort) and therefore the order of the equal output lines. The sort itself is in the na_ungapped.c range.

branch: per init hit: local copy, context offsets, BlastIntervalTreeContainsHSP, cutoff, Blast_HSPInit, Blast_HSPListSaveHSP, BlastIntervalTreeAddHSP
notes: A hit is skipped when its ungapped box is contained by a gapped HSP already in the tree (min_diag_separation 50 for task blastn, 6 for megablast; tree internals belong to the E2 range); otherwise the score-only extension runs, and only a score >= cutoff_score (hit_params->cutoffs[context].cutoff_score = BLAST_Cutoffs for the expect value with the context's eff_searchsp, INT4_MAX for invalid contexts; options->cutoff_score is 0 for blastn) creates the HSP, appends it to the list in processing order, and adds it to the tree (query and subject). tmp_hsp.score is the ungapped score, frame sign +1. LOSAT matches this per hit; low-score and restricted-alignment redo branches are not reached.

branch: megablast (is_greedy): q_off/s_off = ungapped start + length/2, BLAST_GreedyGappedAlignment(score only, compressed subject), start override
notes: The seed is the midpoint of the ungapped extension (Int4 division), the aligner runs on the context query and the packed chunk subject with the chunk length, and the HSP's start point is replaced by greedy_query/subject_seed_start. LOSAT skips the hit when the aligner returns no result; that can only happen for an empty extension range, which a start inside the ungapped box never has (NCBI would return an error status).

branch: task blastn (DP): s_end >= s_off + 8 shifts the start by 3, s_BlastDynProgNtGappedAlignment
notes: The 3-base shift is applied to both q_off and s_off when the ungapped end is at least 8 past the seed (chunk-local coordinates), then the packed DP extension runs with x_dropoff = min(gap_x_dropoff, ungapped score) and the start point kept in the HSP is the shifted seed.

Stores query/subject start and stop, the greedy seed start and the score; keeps the previous edit script only when the new one is NULL, which needs an empty traceback and cannot give a positive score. LOSAT returns the same fields in GreedyGappedCore.

branch: score only (do_traceback FALSE), compressed_subject TRUE, gap costs 0/0 (megablast default)
notes: rem = s_off % 4 for the right extension and 0 for the left, both directions call BLAST_AffineGreedyAlign (which hands 0/0 costs to BLAST_GreedyAlign), max_dist doubled and the direction restarted while the aligner returns a negative value, then score = (q_ext_r+s_ext_r+q_ext_l+s_ext_l)*reward/2 - d*(reward-penalty) with C left-to-right integer division, and the seed estimate (valid_seed_len_l/r from the longest exact run inside the alignment box, ties go to the left). X is gap_x_dropoff unscaled; doubling for odd rewards happens inside the aligner. Verified term by term.

branch: score only, compressed_subject TRUE, affine gap costs; reward odd or even
notes: Same flow with BLAST_AffineGreedyAlign on affine costs; for an odd reward the aligner works on doubled scores and the caller halves the returned score (score /= 2, truncating), for an even reward it is returned as is; the seed estimate is the same.

branch: traceback (do_traceback TRUE, compressed_subject FALSE, rem = 4), gap 0/0 or affine
notes: Both prelim edit blocks reset, right and left extension with the edit blocks, Blast_PrelimEditBlockToGapEditScript, then s_ReduceGaps(esp, query+q_off-q_ext_l, subject+s_off-s_ext_l, query+q_off+q_ext_r, subject+s_off+s_ext_r) on the adjusted subject; the score formula is the same as in score-only mode. Called from the traceback stage on the AdjustSubjectRange subject (run.rs:10958).

Left (rev) block in stored order, right (fwd) block reversed, the two ops next to the start point merged when their types are equal; size 0 gives a NULL script in C (LOSAT builds an empty script) which only happens for a zero-score empty alignment that cannot pass the cutoff. The DP traceback has its own transcription of the merge with the same rule.

Walks back (bf) and forward (af) over the script until the substitution deficit qd/sd is covered, writes the negative filler count, zeroes the ops between, adds bf/af to the current op and rewrites the neighbouring gap op as Del or Ins of |qd-sd|; do-while exit conditions and early returns match, signed Int4 counts kept in i32.

Same compaction: skip zero counts, merge equal ops, copy when a substitution is involved, otherwise cancel the shorter gap against the longer (d > 0, d < 0, d == 0 branches incl. the j == 0 case). In C the d > 0 branch with j == 0 writes esp->num[-1] (undefined); LOSAT would panic there; the case needs two different gap ops with no substitution first in the script, which the greedy tracebacks do not produce.

First pass extends substitution runs of 12 or more over adjacent matches (nm1 backwards bounded by the query start only, nm2 forwards with the post-increment probe and the final q1--/s1--), second pass reduces short gap-sub-gap triples (d == 3 special case, d < 12 with nm1/nm2 and d = min) with the same pointer arithmetic. The subject read before the alignment start is the sentinel in C and a bound in LOSAT (E2c section K); with AdjustSubjectRange shifting the subject it is a real base in C, but reaching it needs an alignment with several thousand net gap letters.

x_dropoff = min(gap_x_dropoff, ungapped score); offset_adjustment = 4 - s_off % 4 added to both q and s starts (back off by 4 when either exceeds its length); left extension reversed, right extension from query+q_length-1 and packed subject+(s_length+3)/4-1 only when both starts are inside; stops = lengths otherwise; score = left + right. LOSAT's guard for a start past the end cannot trigger for valid seeds.

branch: reverse_sequence TRUE (left) and FALSE (right)
notes: Score-only X-drop DP over the packed subject: unpack base A[(M-a)/4] at (a-1)%4 for the reverse case and A[1+(a-1)/4] at 3-(a-1)%4 for the forward case, query bytes read through the BLASTNA matrix (sentinel row/column INT4_MIN/2), MININT = INT4_MIN/2 start values, x_dropoff raised to gap_open+gap_extend, dp_mem growth rules and the window shrink/extend steps all match; int arithmetic wraps like C.

branch: nucleotide (matrix scoring), traceback start when the gapped start is (0,0)
notes: q_length <= 11 returns the HSP midpoint; otherwise the best 11-wide window along the common diagonal, then the window at the HSP end if the best is not positive, else failure (the HSP is dropped). LOSAT also returns no start for an empty range, which an HSP never has. Called only when both gapped starts are 0, as in blast_traceback.c:436.

UNSURE (reachability): offset = min(s_gapped_start - s_hsp_offset, q_gapped_start - q_hsp_offset) is computed in usize in LOSAT but Int4 in C, where it is negative when the gapped start lies left of the preliminary HSP start and q_start = gapped_start - offset then moves right. In release builds equal negative differences wrap to the same result, but a negative difference on one axis and a non-negative one on the other picks a different minimum, and debug builds would panic. A start left of the HSP needs a score-only DP start (seed+3 rounded up to a multiple of 4) followed by mismatches (small -word_size, task blastn); greedy seeds always lie inside the alignment box. The identity-run loops, hspMaxIdentRun 10 and 10*1.5 = 15, the max_offset = index - score/2 rule and the return values match.

branch: subject_length >= MAX_SUBJECT_OFFSET (90000)
notes: Same Int4 arithmetic: max_extension_left = q_off + 3000, right = query_len - q_off + 3000, start_shift and the clipped length; shorter subjects return shift 0 and are untouched.

branch: task blastn (not out-of-frame): ALIGN_EX left from q_start+1/s_start+1, right from q_start+1, gap pruning at both ends
notes: Left extension includes the start point and right excludes it; query_start = q_start - private_q + 1 and query_stop = q_start + private_q + 1; a right extension with zero length leaves stop = start+1 as in C; the edit script is the merged rev+fwd script; leading and trailing non-substitution ops are removed with the start/stop and score corrected by gap_open + num*gap_extend, both ends. The final X-drop (100 bits) is used as gap_x_dropoff, set by the traceback caller.

branch: rem == 4 (uncompressed subject, traceback stage), forward and reverse
notes: Counts matching positions while seq1 < 4 (an ambiguity code in the query always mismatches, including N against N) and seq1 == seq2; reverse indexes len-1-index. Bounds are the sequence lengths in both.

branch: rem != 4 (packed ncbi2na subject, preliminary stage), forward and reverse
notes: Forward reads byte (seq2_index+rem)/4 at 3-(seq2_index+rem)%4, reverse reads byte (len2-1-seq2_index)/4 at 3-(len2-1-seq2_index)%4 without rem (the left extension starts at the byte start, rem = 0); query ambiguity codes (>= 4) never equal a 0..3 base. Same condition order and bounds.

branch: seq2 byte equals FENCE_SENTRY (201) sets fence_hit
notes: A blastn subject (BLASTNA codes 0..15 with 0xF sentinel) never contains 201, so fence_hit stays FALSE in both implementations; the fence returns in the aligners are dead.

branch: gap costs 0/0, score only (edit_block NULL: rolling rows last_seq2_off[d+1] = [d-1])
notes: Checked: xdrop_offset = (X + match/2)/(match+mismatch) + 1, max_score zero fill, first-mismatch early return (index == len1 or len2, d = 0, seed set), the d loop with the four sentinel writes of kInvalidOffset at d-1, xdrop_score = ceil(max_score[d-xdrop_offset] + (match+mismatch)*d - X)/(match/2)) with C's integer match/2 (match is even after the odd-reward doubling), the per-diagonal MAX(k+1,k)+1 then MAX with k-1, the x-drop rejection narrowing diag_lower or writing kInvalidOffset, slide, longest exact run seed, end1/end2 clamping, best update with >= , convergence when diag_lower > diag_upper and -1 when max_dist is exhausted. The two rolling rows reproduce the C aliasing. reward >= 1 is guaranteed (reward <= 0 is rejected), so no division by zero.

branch: gap costs 0/0, with traceback (edit_block set, rows kept in the MB space pool)
notes: Same loop with a new row per distance from the pool ((diag_upper-diag_lower+7)/3 three-int units, origin diag_lower-2), pool rewound per call so stale cells persist as in C; traceback via s_GetNextNonAffineTback (prefer diag-1 only if strictly larger than both others, then diag, else diag+1), substitution runs of seq2 differences (minus 1 for a gap in seq1), then the first run last_seq2_off[0][diag_origin].

branch: odd match score doubles match, mismatch, X, gap open and extend; gap open == gap extend == 0 hands over to BLAST_GreedyAlign
notes: match % 2 == 1 multiplies all five values by 2 before the 0/0 test (megablast default 1/-2 becomes 2/4, X doubled); the 0/0 case calls the non-affine aligner with the doubled values.

branch: affine gap costs, score only (edit_block NULL: last_seq2_off[d] = [d-max_penalty-1])
notes: Checked: op_cost = match+mismatch, gap_extend + match/2, BLAST_Gdb3 gcd reduction of (op_cost, gap_open, gap_extend) with the X threshold not divided, max_penalty = MAX(op_cost, gap_open_extend), scaled_max_dist = max_dist*gap_extend, diag_bounds with kInvalidDiag for negative distances, the open/extend/match candidate offsets for deletions and insertions, xdrop_score clamped at 0, end1_diag/end2_diag handling, strict > for the best score, num_nonempty_dist bookkeeping and the next-distance diagonal ranges. The unconditional diag_lower[d-max_penalty] read at d < max_penalty hits the invalid initial entries (no decrement); LOSAT guards d >= max_penalty, equal.

branch: affine gap costs, with traceback (rows from the pool for d > max_penalty)
notes: Traceback state machine Sub / Ins / Del with s_GetNextAffineTbackFromMatch and FromIndel, best_diag moved by -1 / +1, seq2_index decremented for deletions, final run last_seq2_off[0][diag_origin].match_off; preallocated rows for d <= max_penalty and pool rows after, as in C. Index guards for negative distances stand for the invalid initial diag bounds.
Same comparisons and tie-breaks (>= for the match candidate, > insert over delete, new_seq2_index < match_off for opening a gap, strict > in the non-affine choice).

Memory pool for traceback rows (1,000,000 SGreedyOffset units per block, rewound per call, a new block of max(1e6, request) when full). Only memory and the reuse of stale cells matter and LOSAT models both; a negative request (empty affine range) returns NULL but the row is never read.
calloc of op_type and num; size <= 0 returns NULL in C whereas LOSAT builds an empty script, which only matters for an empty traceback (see Blast_PrelimEditBlockToGapEditScript).

Zero counts ignored; the new count is added to the last op when its type equals last_op (last_op is INVALID after a reset), otherwise a new op is appended. The DP traceback uses gap_edit_ops_add with the same rule on a Vec.
Reset sets num_ops = 0 and last_op = INVALID (LOSAT also clears the vector, never read past num_ops); Append re-adds each op through GapPrelimEditBlockAdd (not called on the blastn path).
Freeing and duplication helpers; no effect on output.

Called by the affine greedy aligner.
